newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks dip in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks dip in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks slipped into negative territory in early Tuesday morning trade with the market digesting recent gains and showing some concern about the trend in the U.S. bond market, brokers said.
"Blue chips are going to consolidate, at least until we see a breakout in the U.S. bond market, said Geoff Galbraith in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
The Hang Seng Index dipped 65 points to 13,802 in early morning trade, recovering slightly from the opening slide to a low of 13,768.14. Turnover was a robust HK$1.16 billion.
"We need to digest recent gains," Galbraith said.
Brokers said Hong Kong investors were watching closely the recent divergence in the performances of the Dow and the U.S. long bond.
On Friday, the U.S. long bond ended up 1/32 at 95-26/32 to yield 6.83 percent, a sideways move, after retreating earlier in the week on fears of a hike in U.S. interest rates.
The U.S. bond market was closed on Monday for a federal holiday.
The New York Stock Exchange was open, however, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced to set its ninth record of the year with a climb of 10.77 points to 6,843.87.
"This is a healthy consolidation," said Patrick Ho, head of Hong Kong and China sales at UBS Securities (East Asia). "Even another 500 points or so would not be a bad thing."
The finance sector led the market down. Properties were also weak.
"Banks came under selling pressure in London overnight and HSBC also was pulled down," said Ho.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings slumped HK$4.00 to HK$180.00 and Hang Seng Bank was sold off HK$1.50 to HK$94.25. Bank of East Asia eased HK$0.50 to HK$36.30.
Henderson Land and Sun Hung Kai Properties both dropped HK$0.75 to HK$75.25 and HK$74.00.
Hang Seng Index futures were struggling, said Ho.
The January contract was down 82 points to 13,755 and the February contract was off 83 points to 13,815 in mid-morning trade.
